svg.aria-label: The arrangement of Exercise 05: one kernel VM running two hardened containers built from the same image. ex05-foothold, the attacker's position, and ex05-neighbour, an uninvolved bystander, share no mount, volume, namespace, network or cgroup by configuration. Both, however, read the image's lower-layer files, including heartbeat.sh, agent.sh, /bin/sh and /usr/bin/su, through the same host inode and therefore the same set of page-cache pages, because both containers were built from one image. That shared page cache is the only channel between them, created by no configuration option and removable by none.
svg.title: The arrangement: two containers, one image, one channel
svg.desc: One kernel VM contains two containers, ex05-foothold and ex05-neighbour, each independently hardened: unprivileged, all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, default seccomp and AppArmor, a read-only root filesystem, uid 65534, and its own mount, PID, network, IPC, UTS and cgroup namespaces, with network_mode none. Nothing is shared between them by configuration; a red divider marks the absence of any common mount, volume, namespace, network or cgroup. Both containers were nonetheless built from the same image, so unmodified files in its lower layers, including heartbeat.sh, agent.sh, /bin/sh and /usr/bin/su, are, on the host, a single inode each, and overlayfs serves both containers' reads from that one inode's page-cache pages rather than a copy per container. That shared page cache, drawn as the one box beneath both containers, is the only channel between them: no configuration option created it, and none can withdraw it.

g.text: TWO CONTAINERS, ONE IMAGE, ONE CHANNEL
kernel VM ("kernel-target")
Nothing below is shared by configuration between the two containers: no common mount, volume, namespace, network or cgroup.
ex05-foothold
Role: the attacker's position, the only container occupied.
Hardened like its neighbour: unprivileged, no capabilities,
its own namespaces, no network.
./shared → /shared
host mount unique to this container, Stage 3's route
Runs:
sleep infinity
Never enters, addresses or references the neighbour;
issues splice4() against its own read-only view of the image.
Full hardening list: Section 9.2.
ex05-neighbour
Role: an uninvolved bystander, an instrument, not a target.
Hardened like the foothold: unprivileged, no capabilities,
its own namespaces, no network.
/tmp/tenant-b/api.key
private tmpfs secret, unreadable from the foothold
Runs:
agent.sh → heartbeat.sh, every 5s
Each tick is a fresh process: /bin/sh re-reads heartbeat.sh's
text from the page cache, so a corrupted page takes effect at once.
Full hardening list: Section 9.2.
reads via overlayfs
reads via overlayfs
IMAGE LOWER LAYERS, ONE HOST INODE PER FILE
/opt/tenant/heartbeat.sh · /opt/tenant/agent.sh · /bin/sh · /usr/bin/su
Unmodified since both containers were built from the same image; overlayfs serves a read of a lower-layer
file from that underlying inode's page-cache pages, not a copy per container; no `docker-compose.yml` option expresses this.
THE ONLY CHANNEL.
A page-cache write issued inside the foothold lands on these same pages,
so the neighbour reads it too, though it shares nothing else with the foothold at all (Sections 9.3.5, 9.5).
